era: Genesis / Sega CD / Dreamcast underwater action-adventure
summary: Appaloosa/Novotrade and Sega's atmospheric dolphin action-adventure series, spanning 16-bit originals, educational spin-offs, and the 3D Defender of the Future reboot.

entries.title: Ecco the Dolphin

emulation.emulator: Sega CD hardware or Genesis Plus GX/Fusion-compatible Sega CD emulation
emulation.notes: Use the Sega CD version for main capture; Genesis/Switch Online paths are cartridge-version alternatives.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sega CD presentation with CD audio.

primary.why: The Sega CD version is the best main route for the first Ecco because it adds a CD soundtrack and version-specific level/checkpoint changes over the cartridge original while preserving the core game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Sega CD/Mega-CD version on original hardware, Sega Genesis Mini 2 if available, or accurate Sega CD emulation for capture. Use Genesis/Nintendo Switch Online only for the cartridge version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ecco the Dolphin: Complete was announced in April 2026, but no platforms or release date were announced, so it is not yet a playable primary.

entries.title: Ecco: The Tides of Time

emulation.emulator: Sega CD hardware or Genesis Plus GX/Fusion-compatible Sega CD emulation
emulation.notes: Use Sega CD for main capture; use Genesis routes for cartridge soundtrack comparison.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Sega CD presentation with CD audio and CG cutscenes.

primary.why: The Sega CD version replaces the cartridge soundtrack with Spencer Nilsen's CD audio and adds CG story cutscenes, making it the highest-production classic route for the sequel.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Sega CD/Mega-CD version on original hardware or accurate Sega CD emulation for capture. Use Genesis/Nintendo Switch Online or Steam only if you specifically want the cartridge soundtrack/version.

entries.remaster_caveats: Ecco the Dolphin: Complete was announced in April 2026 for the first two games, but platforms and release date were not announced.

entries.title: Ecco Jr. and the Great Ocean Treasure Hunt

emulation.notes: Stylus/book input makes original hardware the intended route.

primary.why: The Great Ocean Treasure Hunt is the Pico educational Ecco Jr. title and uses Pico stylus control, with no documented port or modern rerelease.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Sega Pico release on original Pico hardware. Treat video capture/emulation as archival only if hardware capture is impractical.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or port is documented.

entries.title: Ecco Jr.

emulation.emulator: Sega Classics wrapper or Genesis Plus GX
emulation.notes: Use PC if owned; otherwise original/collection routes are fine for this simpler entry.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Genesis/Mega Drive presentation with emulator scaling.

primary.why: The Genesis Ecco Jr. is available through Sega Classics/Steam and keeps the main Genesis game in a capture-friendly wrapper; it is the easiest route when already owned.
primary.how_to_play: Play the owned Steam/Sega Classics version if available. Use Genesis hardware, Wii Virtual Console, or PS2/PSP Sega Genesis Collection if that is the available route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Sega Classics delisting affects new purchase, but existing owners retain access.

entries.title: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future

emulation.emulator: Flycast or Redream; PCSX2 for PS2 comparison
emulation.notes: Use Dreamcast emulation for main capture.

primary.why: Defender of the Future was designed and first released for Dreamcast, with the PlayStation 2 version arriving later; without a sourced definitive PS2-exclusive content case, the Dreamcast original is the main route and upscales well through Dreamcast emulation.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast release on original hardware or Flycast/Redream for upscaled capture. Use PS2 only if that disc/hardware path is easier.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster is documented; the planned sequel Sentinels of the Universe was cancelled.
